subject: Pricing bucket sequencing & safeguard redline negotiation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@veridian.com>, procurement@veridian.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing bucket sequencing & safeguard redline negotiation

Hi Elena / Veridian procurement team —

Following our call last week, attached is the updated order form with the proposed bucket sequencing and the temporary stabilization safeguard we discussed. Two specific items we want to highlight that came from our side: 1) a temporary stabilization surcharge that can apply during a material surge (explicitly capped and with a defined sunset), and 2) a fee-floor to protect minimum-unit economics during the initial ramp.

Key asks from Veridian we want to resolve quickly so legal can prepare the signable:
- Can you confirm whether a surcharge cap expressed as 20% of monthly spend (not to exceed $X) is acceptable?
- Is a 24-month commit window workable in exchange for a 10% concession on list rates?
- Any procurement/finance paperwork we should route with the order form?

I attached RN_OrderForm_v2_edits.docx with inline comments. If you prefer, Marissa from our contracts team is looped to handle redlines directly.

Thanks — aiming to finish redline resolution by end of week so we can push DocuSign.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Attachment: RN_OrderForm_v2_edits.docx (docx)
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@veridian.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridian.com
Date: 2027-10-19T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing bucket sequencing & safeguard redline negotiation

Thanks Sean — quick read-through from our side. Attaching a PDF with inline legal comments. High-level: Veridian is sympathetic to the need for short-term stabilization but our procurement/legal teams cannot accept a unilateral surcharge mechanism without clearer triggers, limits, and a mutual escalation path. Specific items:

1) Surcharge trigger: need to tie to verifiable infra metrics (actual token throughput or average p50 latency/usage) rather than service-owner discretion.
2) Cap & duration: we can accept a temporary surcharge only if it is capped at 10% (not 20%) and auto-expires after 45 days unless mutually re-authorized.
3) Fee floor: we are okay with a modest floor but request a graduated floor for the first two quarters to reflect ramp uncertainty.

We left suggested redlines in Veridian_redline_v1.pdf. From procurement: we are open to the 24-month commit provided the price concession applies to a defined SKU/route and that true-ups happen quarterly.

On the DocuSign / signature flow — we need the finalized legal redline before we can sign. Please have legal review and update.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-19T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing bucket sequencing & safeguard redline negotiation

Elena — really appreciate the clear redlines. I’m Marissa from Redwood’s contracts team; I’ll steward legal edits and try to keep this tight. Quick reply to your three bullets and a suggested compromise below.

1) Trigger mechanics: we can explicitly tie the surcharge to two measurable thresholds (30-day rolling average of per-route token consumption > X and sustained queueing that breaches p90 latency SLA for > 30 minutes). Those thresholds will be documented in the deployment appendix and audited on request.

2) Cap & duration: counter-proposal — cap surcharge at 15% with automatic 30-day sunset and an explicit renewal cadence (mutual written agreement required to extend). Also include a hard cap per calendar month (dollar limit) so you won’t see runaway charges.

3) Fee floor: propose a stepped floor: Q1 = 60% of standard, Q2 = 75%, Q3+ = 100% to reflect ramp and reduce churn risk. True-ups quarterly.

As trade: Redwood will extend the 10% list-rate concession across the committed SKUs for a 24-month term if Veridian accepts the 15% surcharge cap with the defined triggers and sunset. We can also add a buy-down clause that reduces the floor if usage materially exceeds agreed thresholds for sustained periods.

I’ve attached proposed_exhibit_C_redline.docx which contains the exact clause language. If Veridian can live with the 15% cap and the trigger language above, we can prepare a signable PDF and send for signature tomorrow.

Marissa / Sean — thanks for the clear counter-proposal. I reviewed the proposed Exhibit C language with our legal team this morning. We can accept your compromise with two small edits: 1) change the surcharge cap to 14% (midpoint) and 2) add a requirement that any surcharge be surfaced to our billing contact within 24 hours of being applied (we need near-real-time transparency).

If you’re agreeable to 14% and the 24-hour notification window, we will sign the redlined_signable_orderform.pdf and return via DocuSign. I pasted a DocuSign-ready signature link below for convenience.

On Wed, Oct 19, 2027 at 02:30 PM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — really appreciate the clear redlines. I’m Marissa from Redwood’s contracts team; I’ll steward legal edits and try to keep this tight...

We agree to the 24-hour notification requirement — that’s reasonable. I’m marking internally to accept the 14% cap as a final concession in exchange for the full 24-month committed pricing and the quarterly true-up cadence. Sean — can you confirm the DocuSign flow and that finance will honor the committed SKU mapping? Once Elena signs we’ll route execution.

Regards,
Elena Morales
Head of Procurement Operations | Veridian Systems
